facts.fact: The page defines a Marketing Calendar as the tool that turns a marketing strategy into an Action Plan.
facts.quote: A Marketing Calendar turns this strategy into an Action Plan.

facts.fact: The page describes a Traditional Marketing Calendar as one all-inclusive resource for planning every project and campaign in one place, offered as a downloadable full-year template.
facts.quote: One all-inclusive resource to plan every project and campaign in one place.

facts.fact: The page describes a Quarterly Marketing Calendar as breaking the plan into a detailed, robust plan for one quarter at a time, offered as a downloadable template.
facts.quote: Taking your plan and breaking it down into a detailed robust plan for one quarter at a time.

facts.fact: The page describes a Campaign Calendar as a single template for organizing each campaign, with product launch campaigns given as an example.
facts.quote: A single template to organize each campaign (e.g. Product Launch Campaigns).

facts.fact: According to the page, a marketing calendar shows how the budget is spent over the year, which makes outcome expectations more realistic.
facts.quote: It forces you to see how your budget is being spent over the year and be more realistic about what outcomes you can expect given the plan that you have in place.

facts.fact: The page states that a marketing calendar helps check whether the plan avoids over-reliance on one marketing channel.
facts.quote: You can check if you have the right mix of activities in your plan and are not over reliant on one marketing channel.

facts.fact: The site footer states a copyright year of 2021 for Marketing Coach.
